questions.question: Which of the following planets is located between Mars and Saturn in our Solar System?

options.explanation: Earth is located between Venus and Mars.

questions.question: Imagine if the Earth suddenly stopped rotating on its axis, but continued to revolve around the Sun. What would be the most immediate and significant consequence?

options.text: The length of a year would change dramatically.
options.explanation: The length of a year is determined by Earth's revolution around the Sun, not rotation.

options.text: There would be no more seasons on Earth.
options.explanation: Seasons are caused by Earth's tilt and revolution, not rotation.

options.text: One side of the Earth would experience perpetual day, and the other perpetual night.
options.explanation: Without rotation, one side would always face the Sun (day), and the other would never face the Sun (night).

options.text: The Moon would stop orbiting the Earth.
options.explanation: The Moon's orbit is not directly affected by Earth's rotation.

questions.explanation: Earth's rotation on its axis is what causes the cycle of day and night. If rotation ceased, the side of Earth continuously facing the Sun would remain in daylight, while the opposite side would be in perpetual darkness. Revolution causes the year and, along with tilt, seasons, but stopping rotation directly impacts day/night.
questions.hint: Consider the effect of Earth's rotation on day and night cycles.
